_comment: AGENT: always read this file via the task-index-manager skill before reading or writing any task state. System tracker for ai-worldbuilder (ADR 002). Never add tasks for individual worlds here

tasks.title: Concurrent cell prepares keep invalidating each other's readiness validation
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT (design choice). Seen 2026-10-31 on Portswood Rec (53,-42) with neighbour sessions preparing 52,-42/52,-43: `prepare --apply` on one cell changed the readiness revision of neighbouring cells, so a separate prepare then apply was refused 'validation stale' four times; builders had to chain prepare && apply in one shell command. Revision = content_id([POLICY, facts revision, plan_identity]) in lib/journal/cell_readiness.py; I did not find which input changes (suspect vector-map extract rewrite or neighbour plan notes). Questions: should validation of cell A depend on neighbour state at all? Should apply refresh validation itself under the lock? Decide, then fix.

tasks.title: prepare --apply records a duplicate plan_feature on every run (ambiguous legacy plan warning)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT. On 53,-42 repeated `prepare --apply` added a second plan `houses_brickfield_road` for the same 6 houses already planned as houses_brickfield_road_w176633174, with warning 'ambiguous legacy plan ... no readable handoff spec'; a duplicate `houses_kitchener_road` (bare id from the 2026-10-29 build in row -43) also showed planned in 53,-42. I dismissed both with dismiss-feature. Decide whether prepare should skip groups already covered by a spec-backed plan, and how legacy bare ids should be matched.

tasks.title: Feature builds across a cell edge silently invalidate a finished neighbour and may generate ghost cells
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT (policy). Applying houses_kitchener_road_w176634502 (footprint z -5382..-5343) reached 5 blocks into finished cell 53,-43 and marked its trees/decor stale (trees=False, decor=False). An earlier apply also generated a lidar ghost cell at 56,-40 (230k blocks, 'ghost-ground' journal seq 620) that the user did not ask for. Decide: warn/confirm before an apply touches a done neighbour; keep or drop frontier ghost generation on feature applies; whether edge fringe (roof overhang) should invalidate trees/decor at all.

tasks.title: World provider osm_extract.py: ogr2ogr ran without OSM_CONFIG_FILE; duplicates lib/sources
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT. In worlds/southampton-build/providers/geofabrik-hampshire/osm_extract.py run_ogr2ogr passed no --config OSM_CONFIG_FILE, so GDAL 3.13's default schema (no `amenity` on points) failed the furniture preset and blocked `prepare --apply`. I patched it in the world checkout (osm_config(): world downloads/osmconf.ini else TOOL_ROOT/config/osmconf.ini); the patch is uncommitted and has no test, on top of the owner's existing uncommitted edits. The world provider duplicates the presets and run_ogr2ogr in lib/sources/geofabrik_provider.py; decide whether to delete the copy and call the tool one. Also: manifest hints from prepare (`ref_manifest.py add ...` for prepared-53--42 and prepared-54--42, 52,-42, 52,-43) were not run.

tasks.title: Trial: railway run with real rails in a study area (owner picks the stretch)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world and the stretch, and says whether it may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md sections 5 and 6. Owner idea 2026-11-10: real Minecraft rails for long runs of railway, with land height and direction hacking. This is a spike: the deliverable is findings plus a throwaway prototype, not a production builder. Stretch: at least 300 blocks with a curve and a cutting or embankment. Steps: (1) get the railway lines for the area (railway is not in CELL_EXTRACT_LAYERS today; state where they come from, for example a one-off extract from the world's OSM provider) and snap the centreline to a rail-legal path (long cardinal runs, 90-degree corners, diagonals as staircases); (2) take a lidar ground profile along it, smooth and clamp to a gentle gradient (find the real-world figure from a source and cite it), level the corridor with cut or fill and grass side slopes; (3) lay ballast and rails, with one ascending rail only where a step is needed; (4) apply under the site lock with a structure backup and look in game with the owner. First version leaves out bridges, tunnels, road crossings, fences, stations and signals; note where each would be needed. The prototype lives in the scratchpad, or on a task/* branch only if the owner wants to keep it. Game rules to confirm on the current client: rail needs a solid block below, slopes only on straight cardinal runs at 1 block per block, curves flat, diagonals as staircases. Deliver findings in docs/plans/railway.md: what looked right and wrong, blocks changed outside the corridor, minutes and session tokens used (method stated), and a recommendation with the follow-up implementation tasks to file from the findings. Scratch effects and any snags go to the named world's repo; standing up a new world is separate world work. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and table rows; the owner's in-game verdict on whether the run reads as a railway and the corridor looks natural is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Trial: rule-built typology buildings versus per-building specs (owner picks terrace, estate and shop parade)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world and three study streets, and says whether they may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md sections 2 and 6. Today houses use scripts/house_build.py (already a rule-based footprint builder with a small spec) and non-house buildings use a full hand-written spec in site/builds/<name>.json built by feature_build.py. Question: how much of a real district can rules cover well, using footprint, lidar height, OSM tags (building, building:levels, roof:shape) and a small per-district choice of palette and roof form. This is a spike. The prototype generates minimal specs for the existing builders (house_build and feature_build); it does not add a third builder. Baseline is house_build with a minimal spec versus a full feature_build spec for the same buildings. Study streets: a terrace, a semi-detached or detached estate street, a shop parade. Build about 20 buildings per street with the prototype and compare with the current path, noting minutes and session tokens per building (method stated) and what the player sees from the street. Pitched roofs use pitched_roof_states as it is today. Deliver findings in docs/plans/typology-buildings.md: which building classes the rules cover, what still needs a designer, cost per building under each path, and a recommendation, including whether roof and facade detail (I-006) and glazing become class recipes. File implementation tasks from the findings, not before. Scratch effects and snags go to the named world's repo. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and table rows; the owner's in-game verdict on whether the rule-built streets read as the real ones is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Woodland: dense fill, mixed species, understorey and woodland floor
tasks.notes: Deliverable: inside wood polygons, fill towards the aerial canopy cover (about 80%), mixed species and heights, understorey bushes (persistent leaves at Y+1 to Y+2) and ferns, podzol/coarse_dirt/moss_block floor with grass at the edges; labelled inference, removable through the foliage and decor masks. Owner: trees need more density. Feasibility risk: trees apply cost 962 s for 113 trees (about 8.5 s per tree), so an 80% fill is thousands of trees; diagnose the per-tree apply cost first or batch it. Check: wood across the river in cell 63,-45 matches the aerial density; apply time for it stays under a stated limit; owner verdict in game.

tasks.title: Rough grass and mottled ground on non-lawn grass
tasks.notes: Owner request: plain grass on farmland reads bland, the aerial shows mottled ground. Deliverable: new class key ground_texture (add to the validator via the schema pattern). Gate: meadow, farmland, grassland, heath, scrub and nature_reserve only; lawns never (rules in docs/plans/park-rural.md section Rough grass without spoiling lawns). Place from aerial texture variance, seeded per cell and column, removable through the masks and counted in the report. Planting is null when frontage.inference is false and rural has inference false, so use its own key; reuse the flower vocabulary of #266 (REFINE_PLANTS), do not re-implement. OWNER DECISION PENDING: palette shares (starting values in the plan doc, low confidence). Check: farmland cell 87,-48 shows tufts and mottling, park lawns unchanged; owner verdict.

tasks.title: Roof half-height snapping must not erode a pitched ridge crest
tasks.notes:
Cause: full measurement is on issue I-047 (cause text); in short, `snap_lone_odd_half_heights` (introduced by #302; its docstring says it keeps a clean ridge line) lowers a real ridge crest on West from 12 to 6 half-steps over about six rows. Loop 1 (snap a lone odd cell to its nearest same-zone neighbour, then re-cap with `regularise_roof_half_heights`) does most of it: 194 columns, from 116 lone-odd cells going in. Loop 2 (drop a still-lone odd cell one half-step) changes 44 more. A clean drifting ridge is untouched; the trigger is odd float noise on the flanks, which West has plenty of. The owner sees mush with a dipping ridge (S-099). Measured on one roof only; the measurement was read-only (West's pipeline run in memory against the lidar DSM) and reviewed by an independent subagent on 2026-11-21.

Deliverable: a pitched roof's crest keeps its regularised height through the snap, for any ridge (straight, drifting, diagonal) with odd float noise on its flanks. Rule, not a West tweak. Agent suggestion only, loop 1 being the main cause: resolve a lone odd cell without pulling a higher neighbour down (snap upwards when the 2 half-step cliff cap allows, or never let a snap lower a local maximum), then re-cap from the crest.

Check: (1) fixture test, written to fail first on today's code: a ridge of 12 half-steps with +-1 odd noise on the flanks and a crest that shifts a column every 4 rows keeps every row's crest within 1 half-step of its regularised height; the existing speckle tests (test_lone_odd_cell_snaps_to_its_neighbours, the noisy-ridge no-lone-odd test) stay green. (2) After the owner's West rebuild, read the recorded plan's roof tops (the _tops helper in lib/audit/roof_lint.py): the crest on z-5608..-5602 is at or above 11 half-steps. (3) Owner verdict in game on I-047 S-099 (the mush and dip) and S-083.

Covers: I-047 (S-099; S-083 stays open until re-reviewed). May affect I-009 and I-019 on other pitched roofs; not measured.

Not covered: the 4-5-wide strip of mixed bottom-half slabs and full blocks along the crest top, I-022 S-029 (stair gaps) and I-048 S-088 (stairs on the flat black roof). None is explained by this.
